sentence_stem: Having exhausted every avenue of appeal,
correct_completion: the lawyer finally accepted that the verdict could not be overturned.
full_sentence: Having exhausted every avenue of appeal, the lawyer finally accepted that the verdict could not be overturned.
acceptable_variants: the lawyer conceded that no further remedy remained.
the lawyer reluctantly abandoned the case.

options.text: the court was persuaded to reopen the case.
options.why_wrong: This introduces a new development, while the stem presents all options as already used up. Reopening contradicts the sense of a final outcome.

options.text: the lawyer finally accepted that the verdict could not be overturned.
so the verdict was overturned on appeal.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a result, but the stem says every appeal was already exhausted, so an overturned verdict is impossible here.

options.text: had the appeal been filed a week earlier.
options.why_wrong: This is a conditional clause that needs a main clause to follow it. It does not complete the sentence the participle phrase sets up.

grammar_focus: Participle clause expressing a completed action, followed by a main clause with a logical conclusion
explanation: The participle phrase presents a completed situation, so the main clause must state the logical conclusion that follows from it. Only the option describing acceptance of a final verdict fits this logic.
translation: Wyczerpawszy wszystkie możliwości odwołania, adwokat w końcu uznał, że wyroku nie da się podważyć.
